milestones.description: Selberg's initial publication relates sums over Laplace eigenvalues to sums over closed geodesics, in analogy with prime-number explicit formulas.

evidence.claim: zbMATH record: J. Indian Math. Soc. 20, 47-87 (1956).
Initial publication in 1956 dealt with compact Riemann surfaces and the analogy with prime-number explicit formulas.
Calls the trace formula Selberg's best and most important work.

milestones.note: Journal (Journal of the Indian Mathematical Society 20, 1956) is not confirmed by a bibliographic record: Crossref did not return it and zbMATH is blocked. Confidence medium, not high.

milestones.label: Huber on hyperbolic space forms and geodesics
milestones.work: Heinz Huber, Zur analytischen Theorie hyperbolischer Raumformen und Bewegungsgruppen, Math. Ann. 138, 1959
milestones.description: Uses the trace-formula method to relate the spectrum to lengths of closed geodesics.

evidence.claim: Crossref record, Math. Ann. 138 (1959), pp. 1-26.

milestones.note: Content not read; the application is inferred from the title and the standard account of Huber's geodesic counting. Treat as a candidate.

milestones.description: Gives a self-contained account of the formula and the zeta function for compact surfaces.

notes: Selberg 1956 is the only first statement and it rests on Wikipedia, not a bibliographic record (JIMS not found in Crossref; the record is now confirmed in zbMATH 0072.08201). The input's 'prime-number analogy' claim is consistent with the Wikipedia article. No first_application milestone was verified (the Selberg zeta-function use is undated). Derived dates: conceptual 1956 (medium), methodological null, institutional 1976. Thin-3 pass: first statement now rests on the zbMATH record of the 1956 paper (Wikipedia and MacTutor Selberg agree); added Huber 1959 (low-confidence candidate application) and McKean 1972. McKean's birth year (1930) and the open end of his lifespan are from general knowledge. Eichler-Selberg trace formula and the Selberg zeta function (undated here) are related but not listed. No naming milestone found.

milestones.label: Glimm's Yukawa coupling in two dimensions
milestones.work: Glimm, J., Yukawa coupling of quantum fields in two dimensions I, Communications in Mathematical Physics (1967)
milestones.description: Constructs a quantum field model rigorously in two spacetime dimensions, the first constructive existence result of this type.

evidence.claim: Communications in Mathematical Physics record for Glimm's Yukawa paper, year 1967
Wikipedia CQFT article: Glimm and Jaffe showed that many examples exist for dimension below 4

milestones.note: Glimm 1967 is the earliest constructive 2D paper found; it is the first_statement here. Whether a prior construction exists was not checked. Nelson's 1966 quartic paper (conference volume) was not verified.
